title: Scalar localization of a linear category at one element
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\varpi\in R$, and let $R[1/\varpi]$ be the localization of $R$ at the multiplicative set $\{\varpi^n:n\geq0\}$, with its ring map $R\to R[1/\varpi]$. (For $R=\mathcal O_E$ the valuation ring of a finite extension $E/\Ql$ and $\varpi=\varpi_E$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $R[1/\varpi_E]=E$.) Let $\mathcal C$ be an $R$-linear category: every $\Hom_{\mathcal C}(K,L)$ is an $R$-module and composition is $R$-bilinear. The *scalar localization* (*rationalization*) $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ is the category whose objects are those of $\mathcal C$, with

$$
 \Hom_{\mathcal C[1/\varpi]}(K,L)=\Hom_{\mathcal C}(K,L)\otimes_R R[1/\varpi],
$$

composition the $R[1/\varpi]$-bilinear map induced by the $R$-bilinear composition of $\mathcal C$, $(f\otimes a)\circ(g\otimes b)=(f\circ g)\otimes ab$, and identities $\mathrm{id}_K\otimes1$; it is an $R[1/\varpi]$-linear category. The *localization functor* $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ is the identity on objects and sends $f$ to $f\otimes1$; it is $R$-linear. If $\mathcal C$ carries an automorphism $[1]$ (a shift) acting $R$-linearly on Hom modules, then $[1]$ induces the automorphism of $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ given by $K\mapsto K[1]$ and $f\otimes a\mapsto f[1]\otimes a$, and $Q\circ[1]=[1]\circ Q$.
